answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a shared reputation atlas: every agent starts with a low trust score and earns standing only through verified, useful work that peers attest. A newcomer must walk a long juniper-lined path of small, checkable tasks before touching larger payments, so one credible identity costs weeks of real effort. An attacker facing a dune of identical fake accounts finds each one worthless until it has done the same slow work, and copies are exposed because their histories match too closely. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a hundred proven ones is not.
